data.title: Stocktwits Biotech Dealmaker: Gilead, AstraZeneca And Roche Chase Pipeline Expansion Over Buyouts
data.description:
Key points:
  • Gilead Sciences partnered with Vir Biotechnology on Wednesday to discover and develop three drugs aimed at solid tumors.
  • AstraZeneca signed an up-to-$1.5 billion AI collaboration with insitro for MASH and cardiomyopathies. 
  • Roche licensed Rona’s drug candidate, and Zealand Pharma teamed with Generate on AI-designed proteins for differentiated obesity approaches.

Large pharmaceutical companies including Gilead Sciences, Roche and AstraZeneca spent this week securing access to discovery technologies and experimental candidates that address clear biological gaps, instead of large-scale acquisitions of rival firms or approved products.

Obesity and cancer remained the clear focal points, with several of the week’s biggest partnerships aimed at differentiated weight-loss mechanisms or new solid-tumor approaches.

Gilead Partners With Vir For New Cancer Drug Candidates

Gilead Sciences (GILD) partnered with Vir Biotechnology (VIR) on Wednesday to discover and develop three drugs aimed at solid tumors. Vir will handle early discovery, design, and optimization using its AI-enabled protein engineering tools and PRO-XTEN masking technology. Gilead receives exclusive rights to nominate candidates and will lead subsequent development, manufacturing, and commercialization.

Vir is eligible for $90 million upfront—$65 million in cash plus a $25 million equity investment at a premium—plus up to $45 million in near-term preclinical milestones and as much as $1.74 billion in later development, regulatory, and commercial payments, along with tiered royalties. The agreement marks Vir’s second major partnership around its masking platform this year after a previous deal with Astellas and adds to Gilead’s attempts to advance its cancer offerings besides its blockbuster drug Trodelvy.

AstraZeneca Taps Insitro’s AI Platform

AstraZeneca (AZN) signed a worldwide exclusive research collaboration with privately held AI therapeutics company insitro focused on metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) and cardiomyopathies. Insitro will apply its Virtual Human platform, which combines human and cellular data with AI, to identify causal disease biology and advance AstraZeneca-nominated targets through discovery to the development-candidate stage.

AstraZeneca will lead clinical development, regulatory work, and commercialization. Insitro will receive $40 million upfront and is eligible for up to approximately $1.46 billion in discovery, development, and commercial milestones, plus single-digit royalties on potential sales.

Roche, Zealand Pharma Add Differentiated Obesity Approaches

Roche secured exclusive worldwide rights to Rona Therapeutics’ investigational drug candidate which targets a protein predominantly expressed in fat tissues. The drug candidate is designed to selectively reduce visceral and ectopic fat while preserving lean mass—an attractive complement to currently popular obesity drug classes like GLP-1. Rona is eligible for up to $100 million in upfront and near-term payments, up to $1.06 billion in additional milestones, and tiered royalties.

Separately, Zealand Pharma entered a collaboration with Generate Biomedicines (GENB) to design multispecific protein therapeutics for obesity and other metabolic diseases using Generate’s generative AI platform. Generate will lead research through lead-candidate selection for two initial programs, with an option for a third; Zealand will handle clinical development, regulatory submissions, and commercialization. Generate receives $30 million upfront, up to $35 million in early preclinical milestones, and nearly $1.2 billion in total potential milestones, plus royalties.

Pfizer, Galderma Make Platform And Commercial Moves

Pfizer (PFE) partnered with privately-held Enodia Therapeutics on a research collaboration and license for compounds intended to block disease-driving proteins at the point of synthesis. The potential value exceeds $500 million, including an upfront payment, milestones, and royalties; Enodia will run discovery against multiple targets while Pfizer takes over later development and commercialization.

How Did Retail Traders React?

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around SPDR S&P Biotech ETF (XBI) fell from bullish to neutral territory over the past 24 hours, while message volume stayed at normal levels.

XBI has fallen 4% over the past week as part of a broader biotech pullback that began after its mid-August peak near $170, but it is up 22.5% year-to-date.

data.title: Trump mocks popularity of the name Mohammad, common among Muslims
data.description:
By Steve Holland and Kanishka Singh

US President Donald Trump made a joke about the popularity of the name Mohammad in the Muslim world as he mocked Iran's presidency during a campaign speech on Friday.

"You know, if you're in doubt about somebody's name from the Middle East, just say 'Mohammad,'" Trump told a crowd in Dalton, Georgia. "You have about a 65% chance. 'Hello, Mohammad.' I've done it for years now. I've never been wrong."

Mohammad is one of the most common male names among Muslims, who often name their sons after the Prophet Mohammad, the founder of Islam.

Trump made the comment as he was discussing Iran during a rally in a hangar at Dalton Municipal Airport in Georgia, where he campaigned for Republican political candidates ahead of the November 3 midterm elections.

"Iran is the only country where nobody wants to be president," Trump said, then pretended to ask several people named Mohammad whether they wanted the job. Masoud Pezeshkian has been president of Iran since 2024.

The Georgia crowd gave the joke a muted response.

Rights advocates and Muslim advocacy groups have repeatedly criticized Trump for rhetoric that they say demonizes and mocks Muslims, immigrants and ethnic minorities.

He has escalated such rhetoric during the midterm campaign season, particularly against Somali and Muslim Americans including Muslim Democratic ‌US Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed and Representative Ilhan Omar, a Minnesota Democrat who came to the US as a Somali refugee.

Trump repeated his vow that Iran would never get a nuclear weapon, seven months after the United States and Israel launched a war on Tehran aimed in part at crippling its nuclear program.

An annual report by the Council on American Islamic Relations released earlier this year attributed rising Islamophobia in the US in part to Trump's crackdown on immigration and pro-Palestinian protests during his second term.

SAN JOSE, Calif., Oct. 16, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Blaize Holdings, Inc. (NASDAQ: BZAI, NASDAQ: BZAIW) (“Blaize,” the “Company,” “we,” “us,” and “our”), a leader in programmable, energy-efficient AI computing, announced today that its Board of Directors declared a dividend of one one-thousandth of a share of newly designated Series B Preferred Stock, par value $0.0001 per share, for each outstanding share of Blaize common stock held of record on October 26, 2026. The outstanding shares of Series B Preferred Stock will vote together with the outstanding shares of the Company’s common stock as a single class exclusively with respect to any proposal to adopt an amendment to the Company’s certificate of incorporation to reclassify the outstanding shares of the Company’s common stock into a smaller number of shares of such common stock at a ratio specified in or determined in accordance with the terms of any such amendment (a “Reverse Stock Split Proposal”), as well as any proposal to adjourn any meeting of stockholders called for the purpose of voting on the foregoing matter (an “Adjournment Proposal”), and will not be entitled to vote on any other matter, except to the extent required under the Delaware General Corporation Law. Subject to certain limitations, each outstanding share of Series B Preferred Stock will have 1,000,000 votes per share (or 1,000 votes per one one-thousandth of a share of Series B Preferred Stock).

All shares of Series B Preferred Stock that are not present in person or by proxy at any meeting of stockholders held to vote on the above described amendment proposal as of immediately prior to the opening of the polls at such meeting will automatically be redeemed by the Company. Any outstanding shares of Series B Preferred Stock that have not been so redeemed will automatically be redeemed in whole, but not in part, at the close of business on the earlier of (i) the business day established by the Company’s Board of Directors in its sole discretion and (ii) the first business day following the date on which the Company’s stockholders approve an amendment to the Company’s certificate of incorporation to reclassify the outstanding shares of the Company’s common stock into a smaller number of shares of such common stock at a ratio specified in or determined in accordance with the terms of any such amendment.

The Company’s Board of Directors has adopted resolutions providing that the Series B Preferred Stock will be uncertificated. The certificate of designation governing Series B Preferred Stock will provide that shares of Series B Preferred Stock may not be transferred except in connection with a transfer by such holder of any shares of the Company’s common stock held by such holder. In that case, a number of one one-thousandths of a share of Series B Preferred Stock equal to the number of shares of the Company’s common stock to be transferred by such holder will be transferred to the transferee of such shares of common stock.

Further details regarding the Series B Preferred Stock will be contained in a report on Form 8-K to be filed by Blaize with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

data.title: Berkshire's New Trick — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Andrew Bary

Berkshire Hathaway is famous for its value orientation. So why is it betting on Bending Spoons, a quirky and richly priced technology conglomerate? This past week, Berkshire added $330 million in stock on top of the $600 million investment it made in Bending Spoons' initial public offering in July.

Bending Spoons, based in Milan, has assembled a group of technology castoffs, such as AOL and Brightcove. Its unusual name, a nod to psychic powers, comes from the sci-fi classic The Matrix. Its stock is anything but cheap, trading for about 10 times forward sales and more than 30 times estimated 2027 earnings, well above the S&P 500's valuation.

So what has attracted Berkshire, the Warren Buffett creation, to Bending Spoons? A new direction under newish CEO Greg Abel? Berkshire won't say. Berkshire has made tech investments, notably Apple, but it generally won't pay a premium price.

Henry Ellenbogen, founder of Durable Capital Partners, spelled out some of the company's charms at the Barron's July Midyear Roundtable: "We believe Bending Spoons' revenue and Ebitda per employee will continue to compound, allowing the company to drive better organic growth and strong operating leverage."

So far, the move is a big win for both Berkshire and Bending Spoons. The latter's stock jumped 45% in the past week and Berkshire has a paper profit of about $800 million so far.

Write to Andrew Bary at andrew.bary@barrons.com

Last Week

Nasdaq Jitters

Terrible times for the tech-heavy exchange. It was down 4.5% for the week on a variety of fears, ranging from whether AI investments will pay off in the long run to laggard cloud-computing stocks like CoreWeave. Look out below!

Will They? Won't They?

With inflation up 3.7%, the possibility of the Federal Reserve hiking interest rates again has reared its ugly head. But would the Fed raise rates so close to an election? CME Group's Mark Shore says probably not. Historically, from Oct. 1 to Election Day, the Fed didn't act 67% percent of the time. And when it did, it cut rates 67% of the time. Don't touch that dial.

Dimon Says

A busy period of punditry for JPMorgan Chase chief Jamie Dimon. He wrote a Wall Street Journal op-ed called "A Plan for the Western World's Revival." Then, in an earnings report, he opined about the "solid economy" but warned that "large fiscal deficits, sticky inflation, elevated asset prices, rising interest rates and geopolitical conditions continue to shift under the surface." Has he replaced Warren Buffett as a must-read?

Harvard Under Siege

Well, not so fast. The Boston Globe says Harvard's endowment reached "a new peak" at $68 billion this fiscal year, up 20% from 2025. The return: 27%. And amid President Donald Trump's attacks, Harvard also hauled in $1.5 billion from donors. Take that, Ken Griffin.

Next Week

GE Aerospace, General Motors, and Netflix release third-quarter results Tuesday, followed by AT&T, Abbott Laboratories, Lam Research, Meta Platforms, Tesla, and Texas Instruments on Wednesday. Comcast, Lockheed Martin, Procter & Gamble, and Western Digital announce their earnings Thursday, while American Express and SLB close out the week on Friday.

The Census Bureau reports new residential construction data for September. Consensus estimate is for a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 1.3 million privately owned housing starts, slightly more than in August.

The National Association of Realtors reports pending home sales for September. Pending home sales are expected to be flat month over month after a 0.3% rise in August.

S&P Global releases both its Manufacturing and Services Purchasing Managers' Indexes for October. Consensus estimates are for a reading of 55.5 for the Manufacturing PMI and 57.9 for the Services PMI. This compares to readings of 55.9 and 58.8, respectively, in September.

data.title: Anthropic quietly pitches its own AI safety bill to lawmakers, Politico reports
data.description:
Anthropic representatives have quietly pitched Capitol Hill lawmakers on a draft bill to regulate frontier AI safety and security, Politico reported on Friday, citing three people with knowledge of the efforts.

The bill would let the government block a model's release or use only if it poses a foreseeable, imminent risk of more than $1 billion in damages, or of killing or seriously injuring more than 50 people, according to the report.

Here are some details:

  • The risk must stem from the creation or release of a biological weapon, the model evading its developer’s controls or a cyberattack, Politico reported

  • An Anthropic spokesperson told Reuters the bill represents proposals outlined in Anthropic's "Advanced AI Framework" released earlier this year

  • The bill would grant the government the "ability to block or deter dangerous deployments of the most powerful models," and also requires developers to test frontier AI models, be transparent about findings, and get them independently evaluated, the spokesperson said

  • The Department of Commerce did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment

  • Under the bill, independent evaluators, which would register with the Commerce Department, would be tasked with periodically evaluating the lab and its frontier models, according to the report

  • The labs could pay these evaluators, provided the payment is not tied to the evaluation's outcome, the report said

  • If the evaluators determine there is “imminent enumerated risk” for a company’s frontier models, they must report it to Commerce within 72 hours of completing their assessment, Politico reported

  • While the Commerce Department could request a judge to halt a model after determining risk, the language explicitly prohibits any other US government department, agency, or officer from suspending development, deployment, or internal use, according to the report

  • A federal judge for the District Court for the District of Columbia could order the suspension of a model, the report said

data.title: Market View — Barrons.com
data.description:
This commentary was issued recently by money managers, research firms, and market newsletter writers and has been edited by Barron's.

Don't Give Up on Bonds

Perspective Capital Investment Services Sept. 30: If the bond market had a voice, we suspect it would be singing the 1970s song "Don't Give Up on Us, Baby."

Sentiment toward bonds has become so negative that we have even seen commentators describing them as among the most hated investment assets in the world.

Short-term bonds have largely avoided the carnage experienced elsewhere in the bond market. Even so, year-to-date total returns (income received plus changes in bond prices) have been flat to slightly down.

Ironically, the very rise in yields that has caused bond price declines (bond prices move inversely to yields) has also improved the future return prospects for bond investors. For shorter-term bonds, in particular, today's higher yields represent a much more attractive risk/reward proposition than witnessed in years.

Historically, current bond yield levels have been one of the strongest indicators of future bond returns. Put simply, when investors begin with higher yields, they have generally gone on to earn higher returns.

In addition to their improving risk/reward profile, we expect the higher-quality bonds we own to fulfill an important diversification role within portfolios. While no asset class works perfectly in every environment, bonds paired with durable-growth stocks can help prevent temporary stock market setbacks from becoming life-changing investment losses.

With concentration in stock markets around the world increasingly hitched to the AI-buildout wagon, diversification may prove more elusive than many investors expect. Don't give up on higher-quality bonds!

Paul A. Muzzey

Carry-Trade Risk is Growing

Commentary Centre Street Cambridge Oct. 15: The AI gamble is on view for all. But there is another, possibly larger wager that has been happening largely away from public eye: the so called "carry trade." If you can borrow money at a low rate and invest the proceeds at a higher rate, you can mint money on the difference; this is the basic business of banks. The risk lies in the possibility that the relative rates may change, making the operation unprofitable....

Another type of carry trade doesn't enjoy such safeguards, namely borrowing in the currencies of countries where rates are low, and lending or investing in countries/currencies offering higher returns. The most popular of these transactions involves the Japanese yen and the U.S. dollar. A 30-year period of a relatively stable currency vis-à-vis the dollar and interest rates of less than 1% have encouraged borrowing in yen to invest in dollars. The outstanding amount of such trades is now estimated at between $2 trillion and $3 trillion.

Unexpected shifts in exchange or interest rates can cause panic where so much money is exposed. This happened briefly in the summer of 2024. A change in central bank policy triggered a massive unloading of stocks, with the Japanese market dropping 12% in one day; the S&P 500 dropped 3%. The risks are enhanced now that Japanese economic activity has improved, and the country's interest rates are rising. A big unwinding of the carry trade could result in the sale of U.S. assets, including large amounts of Treasury securities. That would almost certainly result in higher borrowing costs and have an impact on the equity markets, as well. It is the risks we don't know that can really bite.

Dennis Butler

Where to Hide if Stocks Slide

Paulsen Perspectives Substack Oct. 15: Much of the current stock market appears far less connected to its bull market leadership (technology and communication stocks) than was the case in 2000. That is, most stocks currently exhibit much lower price betas [price sensitivity] to the movements in New Era stocks than they did near the top of the dot-com bull market. Encouragingly, this suggests the contemporary stock market may be far more buffered against any coming period of significant liquidation among New Era stocks than it was during the dot-com bust....I am encouraged that the current price beta of S&P 500 Old Era sectors to New Era sectors is currently zero, suggesting there may be several places to hide out during any pending New Era collapse.

Jim Paulsen

What's Ailing Korea's KOSPI?

Chart of the Day LPL Financial Oct. 14: The KOSPI [Korea Composite Stock Price Index] and Nasdaq Composite have generally moved in the same direction, but the magnitude of their swings has differed. Korea's market is particularly sensitive to the memory industry, leaving the KOSPI more exposed to changing sentiment surrounding DRAM and other AI-related memory products.

Both indexes staged powerful recoveries from their March lows as risk appetite returned and enthusiasm around AI accelerated. However, that concentration became a liability when AI sentiment weakened in June, contributing to a much sharper unwind in the KOSPI as crowded positioning and leverage across memory stocks reversed.

Both markets subsequently recovered, but their paths diverged over the past month. The NDX pushed to new highs as strong second-quarter earnings across the broader AI ecosystem reinforced confidence in the secular AI investment cycle. However, the KOSPI started to break down, with momentum deteriorating and the index falling back below its 200-day moving average.

Competitive concerns within the memory market have added to the pressure. China's ChangXin Memory Technologies, or CXMT, the fourth-largest DRAM producer, has outlined plans to begin production of new DRAM technology this year, raising concerns about additional supply and greater competition for memory leaders.

data.title: Conduent to Pay $80M to Settle Data-Breach Class Action
data.description:
By Elias Schisgall

Conduent agreed to pay $80 million to resolve a class action stemming from a 2025 data breach.

The company will put the $80 million into a settlement fund for plaintiffs to recover legal costs, as well as the costs of credit- and medical-data monitoring, it disclosed in a Friday filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

Conduent disclosed in April 2025 that a "threat actor" had exfiltrated files associated with some of its clients containing personal information related to their end-users.

The company said Friday that it maintains cyber insurance and that the settlement isn't expected to impact its operations or financial position.

The settlement, which is pending court approval, releases Conduent from claims related to the cybersecurity incident.

The company continues to deny fault or liability.

Shares of Conduent were up 1.4%, to $1.41, in after-hours trading.

data.title: Soy barge bids steady-firm as sales to China pick up
data.description:

The first half of 2026 marked a significant transition for VCI Global following the separation and divestment of its capital markets consultancy, fintech and other non-core businesses. The Company is now concentrating its resources and capital allocation on building AI computing capabilities, commercializing AI services and developing infrastructure opportunities across the AI value chain.

At the same time, VCI Global is pursuing complementary opportunities in renewable energy, energy storage and carbon assets as it works toward a broader infrastructure model connecting AI, computing, energy and sustainability.

  • Total equity increased 19.2% to US$114.70 million as of June 30, 2026, compared with US$96.21 million as compared to December 31, 2025.
  • Total liabilities declined 17.7% to US$17.03 million from US$20.69 million over the same period.
  • Cash and bank balances rose more than fivefold to US$5.19 million from US$0.94 million, supported by financing activities and the disposal of an investment.
  • Revenue was US$2.56 million, compared with US$18.74 million in 1H2025, reflecting the Group’s portfolio restructuring and changes in its operating profile.
  • VGAIN Compute was launched, providing customers with a platform to purchase AI tokens and access multiple supported large language models, including OpenAI GPT, Kimi, Meta Llama and Qwen.
  • Acquisition of the controlling stake in PT Fine Carbon Credit Indonesia (FCCI), an Indonesian carbon asset platform associated with approximately 241,000 hectares of forestry areas across four project sites.

“The first half of 2026 represents an important inflection point for VCI Global as we reposition the Company around AI infrastructure and scalable technology services,” said Ang Zhi Feng, Chief Financial Officer of VCI Global. “While revenue declined as a result of the transition, we ended the period with higher total equity, lower liabilities and an increased cash balance. Our priority is to manage liquidity carefully and allocate capital to initiatives with clear commercial potential as we advance our AI services and infrastructure strategy.”

REVENUE REFLECTS PORTFOLIO RESTRUCTURING

The first half of 2026 represents a fundamental change in VCI Global’s operating profile.

The Company has completed the separation and divestment of its capital markets consultancy, fintech, and other non-core businesses, reducing exposure to businesses that were not aligned with its longer-term technology and infrastructure strategy.

Revenue for 1H2026 was US$2.56 million, compared with US$18.74 million in 1H2025. The decrease primarily reflects businesses that have since been separated or divested, along with the transition to a more focused AI infrastructure and technology operating model.

CASH POSITION AND CAPITAL ALLOCATION

As of June 30, 2026, total equity increased 19.2% to US$114.70 million from US$96.21 million at December 31, 2025, while total liabilities declined 17.7% to US$17.03 million from US$20.69 million.

Cash and bank balances increased to US$5.19 million from US$0.94 million at year-end 2025. The increase was supported by financing activities and the disposal of an investment.

The Company intends to prioritize capital deployment based on commercial demand, financing availability and project readiness, with investment priorities spanning AI Infrastructure, GPU computing and related infrastructure.

VGAIN COMPUTE: FROM AI ACCESS TO AI CONSUMPTION

VCI Global announced the launch of VGAIN Compute on October 6, 2026, through its subsidiary V Gallant Limited.

The platform enables users to purchase AI tokens to access supported large language models, including OpenAI GPT, Kimi, Meta Llama and Qwen. Announced applications include content generation, coding, research, business applications and workflow automation.

The platform introduces a customer-facing offering through which VCI Global can pursue revenue from AI services. Its token-based model provides a mechanism for charging users for access to supported AI capabilities.

The broader market opportunity is expanding as businesses move AI from experimentation into production. Gartner forecasts worldwide AI-optimised IaaS spending of US$42.3 billion in 2026, rising to US$66.1 billion in 2027. Gartner also estimates that global spending on AI inference infrastructure will reach US$23.3 billion in 2026, exceeding the US$19 billion forecast for AI model training infrastructure.

The Company’s next priorities include expanding platform usage, evaluating additional models and developing enterprise and developer applications.

DEVELOPING AN INTEGRATED POWER–AI–CARBON ECOSYSTEM

VCI Global’s longer-term infrastructure strategy extends beyond computing capacity to the resources required to support the expansion of AI infrastructure, including electricity generation, solar power, energy storage and data center operations.

The Company intends to develop an integrated infrastructure model designed to connect energy supply with computing demand, with the objective of improving power availability, supporting scalable AI computing and enhancing long-term operating efficiency.

As AI workloads become increasingly compute-intensive, access to reliable and scalable power is becoming an increasingly important consideration in the development of data center and GPU infrastructure. VCI Global believes that combining computing infrastructure with energy development can provide greater control over critical infrastructure requirements as its AI businesses expand.

LONGER-TERM OPPORTUNITIES IN ENERGY AND FOREST CONSERVATION

VCI Global announced that V Gallant had entered into a definitive agreement to acquire a 70% stake in PT Fine Carbon Credit Indonesia (FCCI), a platform associated with approximately 241,000 hectares of forestry areas across four project sites in Indonesia.

The proposed acquisition provides a potential basis for developing forestry-linked carbon credit projects, subject to transaction completion and applicable technical, legal and regulatory requirements.

The voluntary carbon market offers a potential monetization route for eligible forestry projects, but credit prices vary significantly according to project type, certification standard, carbon integrity, vintage, and buyer demand.

According to Ecosystem Marketplace’s 2025 State of the Voluntary Carbon Market report, based on 2024 transactions, the average price was approximately US$14.97 per tonne of CO₂ equivalent for improved forest management credits and US$20.44 for tree-planting and restoration credits. Some premium credits may command prices above US$50, depending on their characteristics and market conditions.

COMMERCIAL PRIORITIES AND INVESTOR MILESTONES

VCI Global’s initiatives cover several potential sources of revenue, each with different development requirements.

  • AI services: VGAIN Compute provides a live platform through which the Company can pursue paid AI model access. Commercial performance can be assessed through active paying users, token consumption, revenue and service delivery costs.
  • GPU cloud services: VGAIN Cloud is intended to support demand for AI computing. Relevant milestones include infrastructure deployment, available GPU capacity, customer contracts, utilisation and revenue generated from computing services.
  • AI data center infrastructure: Galatron AI Factory’s initial planned 5MW deployment provides a defined development milestone within the broader 500MW roadmap. Progress will depend on site readiness, power availability, funding and customer demand.
  • Energy infrastructure: Potential revenue opportunities depend on the development and ownership of specific projects, available generation or storage capacity, and contracted demand.
  • Carbon assets: FCCI represents a potential forestry-linked carbon credit opportunity. Key milestones include transaction completion, project qualification, credit issuance and actual sales.

These indicators provide a clearer basis for evaluating the Company’s progress than global market growth alone.

OUTLOOK

The global expansion of AI infrastructure presents opportunities across model access, cloud computing, data center development and supporting energy infrastructure. VCI Global has announced initiatives across these areas, beginning with the launch of VGAIN Compute and extending to planned computing infrastructure and complementary asset opportunities.

The Company’s ability to benefit from these markets will depend on execution and commercial validation. Market forecasts indicate the scale of industry investment, but they do not establish VCI Global’s future revenue, market share or profitability.

VCI Global intends to progress its initiatives in phases, with the commercial outcomes of each business dependent on customer demand, operating performance, capital availability, project milestones and applicable regulatory requirements.

“Our ambition is to build an AI infrastructure business that connects customer demand, computing capacity and the energy required to support it,” said Victor Hoo, Group Chief Executive Officer and Executive Chairman of VCI Global. “VGAIN Compute provides a commercial entry point for building customer relationships and recurring usage, while our infrastructure strategy creates opportunities to participate more deeply in the AI value chain. Over the longer term, we see the potential to develop an integrated model in Asia that brings together AI computing, energy and forest conservation.”

“We intend to demonstrate the value of this transition through execution. That means growing customer usage, bringing productive computing capacity into service and converting commercial opportunities into revenue. Those are the milestones that will define the next phase of VCI Global.” He added.

Management will continue to emphasize commercial validation, disciplined capital allocation and phased execution. The pace of development and contribution from individual initiatives will depend on customer demand, funding, regulatory considerations and project milestones.

About VCI Global Limited

VCI Global Limited is transforming into an AI infrastructure and technology group focused on AI computing, GPU infrastructure and AI token services through its businesses, including V Gallant and VGAIN Compute. Following the spin-off and divestment of its capital markets consultancy, fintech and other non-core businesses, the Company is sharpening its focus on AI-driven growth while exploring complementary opportunities in renewable energy, power generation, energy storage and forest conservation, including potential carbon credit initiatives. Through these interconnected areas, VCI Global aims to build a scalable and sustainable infrastructure platform supported by disciplined capital allocation and long-term value creation.

data.title: Anthropic signs lease for first Canadian data center
data.description:
Anthropic has signed a lease with EverWind for data center capacity at Point Tupper, Nova Scotia, marking the Claude maker’s first data center agreement in Canada, a company executive said on Friday.

Here are some more details:

  • Separately, EverWind unveiled plans to invest more than C$10 billion in the data center campus and wind power projects in Nova Scotia, calling it the largest privately funded investment in the province’s history.

  • Data centers have faced criticism over their heavy power and water use and the strain they place on local infrastructure.

  • Jacob Glick, Anthropic’s head of public policy for Canada, said the company would protect ratepayers and water resources while ensuring local communities benefit.

  • Anthropic spent $7.33 billion on computing and infrastructure last year, a threefold surge from 2024.

  • The company is preparing for a US IPO that could value it at more than $2 trillion, although New York City Comptroller Mark Levine has urged it to delay the offering over safety and governance concerns.

data.title: XCF Global CEO Updates Shareholders Following Recent Market Volatility
data.description:
HOUSTON, TX / ACCESS Newswire / October 16, 2026 / XCF Global, Inc. today shared the following update with shareholders:

"We understand that the recent volatility and decline in our share price have been concerning and frustrating for our shareholders, and we take those concerns seriously. We value the confidence our shareholders have placed in XCF and believe it is important to communicate openly about the progress we are making and the priorities that continue to guide us.

Although short-term market movements are outside our control, we remain firmly focused on what we can control: executing our strategy, managing our resources responsibly, strengthening our business, and creating sustainable long-term value for our shareholders.

Over the past several months, we believe XCF has made meaningful progress in transitioning our Reno facility from development and commissioning to commercial operations. We reported more than $10 million in revenue for August and over $12 million in gross product sales (a non-GAAP financial measure) for September, with daily production reaching approximately 85,000 gallons by the end of September. These milestones reflect tangible progress in building our business and the dedication of our team. We believe this progress positions XCF to respond to continued growth in demand for renewable fuels, supported by the expansion of low-carbon fuel programs across a growing number of states.

Today, we also announced the closing of our business combination with Southern Energy Renewables and DevvStream, as we work toward advancing our broader strategy to build a diversified energy platform.

We recognize that operational progress must ultimately translate into sustainable profitability, greater financial strength, and long-term shareholder value. Our management team and Board remain focused on these priorities, including disciplined capital allocation, responsible management of our capital structure, and protection of our shareholders' long-term interests.

We know that shareholder confidence is earned through execution, transparency, and results. We are holding ourselves to that standard and intend to demonstrate our progress through measurable operating performance and clear, consistent communication.

On behalf of our management team and Board of Directors, I thank our shareholders for their continued engagement and support. We remain focused on building a stronger XCF and creating long-term value for those who have invested in our future. Our responsibility is not simply to grow the business, but to ensure that the value created by that growth benefits our shareholders over the long term."

Chris Cooper

Chief Executive Officer

XCF Global, Inc.

About XCF Global, Inc.

XCF Global, Inc. is a U.S.-based producer of renewable diesel and SAF focused on decarbonizing transportation while supporting domestic fuel supply, energy security and alternative uses for agricultural waste products. Its New Rise Renewables Reno facility has permitted nameplate capacity of 38 - 40 million gallons per year. XCF trades on the Nasdaq Capital Market under the symbol SAFX. To learn more, visit xcf.global.
